on 20 September, 2025

Author: Madhav J. Jamdar
Bench: Madhav J. Jamdar

In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Anticipatory Bail Application No. 2598 Of 2023

 Versus
 The State of Maharashtra ...

sentences.text:
Responden
 Mr. Pranav Pokale through V.C. a/w Chinmay Sawant, for the
 Applicants.
 Mr. C.D. Mali, App, for the Respondent-State.
 Mr. Eknath Patil, Psi, Pune Rural Police Station, Pune, present.
 Coram: Madhav J. Jamdar, J.
 Dated : 20th September, 2025
 Pc:-
 1.

Mr. Pokale, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicants  tenders unconditional apology for his absence on 19 th September  2025 and he states that voluntarily he will pay Rs.5,000/- as  donation to the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa.

entities.text: Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The  learned Counsel states that the said donation will be paid within  a period of one week from today.
The said statement is accepted  as undertaking given to this Court.

273, 188 of the Indian Penal Code as well as under Sections  26(2)(i), 26(2)(a), 27(3), 59(iii) of the Food Safety and  Standard Act, 2006.
 3.

sentences.text: As per the prosecution case, on 24 th June, 2023 near  Morwadi, Post Kikavi, Taluka Bhor a tempo was intercepted.
Co-  accused were found transporting huge quantity of contraband  articles - gutkha pan masala.

During the investigation it was  found that the said vehicle of the ownership of the Applicant No.
 1 and the Applicant No. 2.
 4.
Perusal of the record shows that the co-accused who was  allegedly the owner of the contraband articles was granted pre-  arrest bail by the Learned Sessions Court.
The record further  shows that a Learned Single Judge by order dated 25 th  September 2023 has granted pre-arrest bail to the Applicants  and the said order is continued till date.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Counsel appearing for the Applicants states that  the issue regarding applicability of Section 328 of the Indian  Penal Code, 1860 to such offences is pending in the Hon'ble  Supreme Court.
 6.
Accordingly case is made out for granting Anticipatory  Bail.

However, learned APP submits that Applicant No. 1 has one  antecedent and the same has not been disclosed in the  Anticipatory Bail Application.
 7.
Mr. Pokale, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicants  fairly submits that the said antecedent has not been mentioned  in the Anticipatory Bail Application.

He states that fresh  Anticipatory Bail Application will be filed on behalf of Applicant  No. 1 by giving particulars of the antecedents and therefore,
 seeks withdrawal of the Anticipatory Bail Application as far as  Applicant No. 1 is concerned.

8. Accordingly, the Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed  of by passing following orders :-
Sudhakar Kalyan Pansare And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180077798/
3  ORDER Page 3 Akash Tayde 4-ABA-2598-2023.DOC

entities.text: Sudhakar Kalyan Pansare And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (a) As far as Applicant No. 1 - Sudhakar Kalyan Pansare the Anticipatory Bail Application is allowed to be withdrawn with liberty to file fresh Anticipatory Bail Application by incorporating particulars of the antecedents.

(b) In the even of arrest of the Applicant No.2 - Dinesh Kalyan Pansare in C.R. No.260 of 2023,
registered with Rajgad Police Station, Pune Rural, Pune, the Applicant No.2 be released on bail on furnishing PR Bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one or two sureties in the like amount.

(c) The Applicant shall attend the Rajgad Police Station, Pune Rural, Pune on 29 th September 2025, 30th September 2025 and 1st October 2025 between 11:00 a.m. to 02:00 p.m. and thereafter as and when necessary.

entities.text: Rajgad Police Station, Pune Rural, Pune
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: (d) The Applicant shall furnish his cell phone number and residential address to the Investigating Officer and shall keep the same updated, in case of any change thereto.

Page 4 Akash Tayde 4-ABA-2598-2023.DOC (e) The Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such a person from disclosing the facts to the Court or to any Police personnel.
(f) The Applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and shall not contact or influence the Complainant or any witness in any manner.
(g) The Applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court.
9. The Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed of in above terms.
